course_info.faculty: Faculty of Engineering and Natural Sciences

catalog_course_description: This course offers a hands-on introduction to quantum programming, focusing on both the theoretical foundations of quantum computing and the practical implementation of the covered concepts. Topics include the distinction between classical and quantum bits, superposition, entanglement, and quantum gates. It covers basic quantum communication protocols and illustrates the power of quantum computing through representative algorithms for search, decision, and factorization problems.
course_learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a basic but solid understanding of the theory of quantum computation.
Create quantum circuits and simulate them in classical simulators.
Write codes for elementary quantum algorithms and execute them in simulators.
Acquire the necessary knowledge to program a gate-based quantum computer.
Analyze and compare classical and quantum algorithmic complexity for specific problems.
